description: Illustrative example for docs/attribution-batch-engine.md. NOT an active proposal awaiting apply. Real batches are produced by an evidence sprint per docs/naming-attribution-automation.md, not hand-written here.

source_refs: Hooper & Whyld, Oxford Companion to Chess (1984), entry 'Réti Opening'.

fields.attribution_source: Hooper & Whyld, Oxford Companion to Chess (1984), entry 'Réti Opening'.
fields.historical_notes: Named for Richard Réti (1889–1929), who championed 1.Nf3 in the 1920s — notably defeating Capablanca with it at New York 1924.

source_refs: Hooper & Whyld, Oxford Companion to Chess (1984), entry 'Bird's Opening'.

fields.attribution_source: Hooper & Whyld, Oxford Companion to Chess (1984), entry 'Bird's Opening'.
fields.historical_notes: Named for the English master Henry Edward Bird (1829–1908), a lifelong exponent of 1.f4.

source_refs: Hooper & Whyld, Oxford Companion to Chess (1984), entry 'Larsen's Opening'.

fields.attribution_source: Hooper & Whyld, Oxford Companion to Chess (1984), entry 'Larsen's Opening'.
fields.historical_notes: Named for the Danish grandmaster Bent Larsen (1935–2010), who employed 1.b3 at the top level in the 1960s–70s.
